problems.title: Skew pairs among tetrahedron edges
problems.question: How many skew line pairs are formed by the six edge lines of a tetrahedron?
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Adjacent edges meet; opposite tetrahedron edges are skew.
steps: The opposite pairs are AB–CD,AC–BD,AD–BC. There are three.

problems.title: A line and its forty-five-degree projection
problems.question: A line makes 45° with a plane; its projection makes 45° with an in-plane line a. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\cos\gamma=\cos45°\cos45°=1/2$.
steps: The smaller line angle is arccos(1/2)=60°.

problems.title: Order mixed-unit trigonometric values
problems.question: Order a=sin4,b=tan95°,c=cos7, with unmarked angles in radians.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Use the correct angle units and quadrants.

problems.title: An identity cancels every term
problems.question: Simplify sin(α−90°)−cos(180°+α)+sin(α+β)[1/cos²β−1−tan²β].
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\sin(\alpha-90°)=-\cos\alpha$, $\cos(180°+\alpha)=-\cos\alpha$, $\sec^2\beta=1+\tan^2\beta$.
steps: The first two terms cancel, and the bracket is zero. The result is 0 on the original domain cosβ≠0.

problems.title: Space diagonals of a heptagonal prism
problems.question: How many space diagonals has a seven-sided prism?
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: From each of n bottom vertices, n−3 top vertices are not on a common face with it.
steps: The count is n(n−3)=7×4=28. Each diagonal is counted once from its bottom endpoint.

problems.title: Combine cosine and a squared sine
problems.question: Find the least positive period of cos4x+sin²2x.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
steps: The function is 1/2+(1/2)cos4x, so its least period is 2π/4=π/2.

problems.title: Project an inclined prism section
problems.question: A plane through a right triangular prism’s base edge makes 30° with the base and cuts a triangular section of area 4√3. Find base area.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Projection area = section area × cosine of the plane angle.
steps: The triangular section’s third vertex lies on the opposite vertical edge, so its orthogonal projection is the entire base triangle.

problems.title: Sine of a principal arccosine
problems.question: Evaluate sin(arccos(−0.6)).
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Arccos returns an angle in [0,π], where sine is nonnegative.

problems.title: A trig sum reaches its amplitude
problems.question: Count roots of √3sinx+cosx=2 in [0,2π].
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x=2\sin(x+\pi/6)$.
steps: Require sin(x+π/6)=1, giving x=π/3+2πk. Only x=π/3 lies in the interval.

problems.title: A vertical section of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: All tetrahedron edges are 1. A plane through the midpoint of a lateral edge is perpendicular to the base and parallel to the opposite base side. Find the triangular section area.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Regular tetrahedron height $H=\sqrt{2/3}$; use similar triangles in the base.
steps: Take base vertices A=(0,√3/2,0),B=(−1/2,0,0),C=(1/2,0,0) and apex D=(0,√3/6,H). The midpoint of AD has y=√3/3,z=H/2.
The vertical section plane is y=√3/3. It cuts AB and AC one third of the way from A, so its horizontal base has length 1/3.

problems.title: Surface area of a regular triangular frustum
problems.question: A regular triangular frustum has base sides 1,2. A lateral edge makes 60° with an adjacent large-base edge. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: The horizontal lateral-edge component along that base edge is half the side difference, (2−1)/2=1/2.
steps: If lateral edge length is L, its component gives L cos60°=1/2, so L=1. Each lateral face has bases 1,2 and legs 1, giving face altitude √(1−1/4)=√3/2.
The three lateral areas sum to 9√3/4. The two equilateral base areas sum to 5√3/4. Total=14√3/4=7√3/2.

problems.title: Factor and sign-chart a sine inequality
problems.question: Solve sin2x+sinx<0.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\sin2x+\sin x=\sin x(2\cos x+1)$.
steps: In one cycle (0,2π), opposite signs occur on (2π/3,π) and (4π/3,2π). Every factor zero is excluded by strictness.
Repeat these intervals with period 2π.
problems.answer: $x\in(2\pi/3+2\pi k,\pi+2\pi k)\cup(-2\pi/3+2\pi k,2\pi k),\ k\in\mathbb Z$.

problems.title: A square pyramid inside a unit cube
problems.question: A pyramid’s base is one face of a unit cube and apex the centre of the opposite face. Find lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: The pyramid height is 1,base side 1; face slant height $l=\sqrt{1+(1/2)^2}=\sqrt5/2$.
steps: Four triangular faces give lateral area=4×(1/2)×1×l=2l=√5.

problems.title: Factor a parameter quadratic in sine
problems.question: For which a does sin²x+(2a+1)sinx+a²+a=0 have a real root?
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: The expression factors as $(\sin x+a)(\sin x+a+1)$.
steps: The first factor can vanish iff −a∈[−1,1], or a∈[−1,1]. The second can vanish iff −a−1∈[−1,1], or a∈[−2,0].
Their union is [−2,1].

problems.title: A radical inequality holds everywhere
problems.question: Solve √(x²+2)>x−1.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\sqrt{x^2+2}>|x|\ge x>x-1$ for all real x.
steps: The radicand is always positive, and the displayed chain proves the inequality without any extraneous squaring step.

problems.title: Homothety about a point off the origin
problems.question: Apply homothety centred at (0,1),coefficient 2,to y=−2x+3. Find the image line.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Image coordinates satisfy $X=2x$, $Y=1+2(y-1)=2y-1$.
steps: Substitute x=X/2: Y=2(−X+3)−1=−2X+5.

problems.title: Equal sum and difference lengths
problems.question: Nonzero vectors a,b satisfy |a+b|=|a−b|. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
steps: The equality makes a·b=0. Since both vectors are nonzero, their angle is 90°.

problems.title: Inclination to the coordinate plane
problems.question: Find the angle between vector (1,2,−2) and the xy-plane.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Line-plane sine = absolute normal component/vector length.
steps: Length=√(1+4+4)=3 and normal component magnitude=2. The angle is arcsin(2/3).

problems.title: Centroid vector relative to an arbitrary point
problems.question: M is centroid,BN a median,KN=a,KB=b, with K any point in space. Express KM.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $BM:MN=2:1$ so M is two thirds of the way from B to N.

problems.title: Exactly two sixes in four rolls
problems.question: A fair die is rolled four times. Find probability of exactly two sixes.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Binomial probability $\binom42(1/6)^2(5/6)^2$.

problems.title: Choose positive counts of three sweets
problems.question: Choose ten sweets of three types, at least one of each. Count selections by type counts.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Positive integer solutions of u+v+w=10 number $\binom{10-1}{3-1}$.
steps: Reserve one of each, then distribute seven identical remaining choices among three types. Stars and bars gives 9 choose 2=36.

problems.title: At least one neighbouring volume
problems.question: Ten distinct book volumes are randomly ordered. Find probability volume 1 is beside volume 2 or volume 3.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Use inclusion–exclusion for the two adjacency events.
steps: Each specified pair is adjacent with probability 2×9!/10!=1/5. Both events occur when volume 1 is between 2 and 3, a block with two internal orders. Probability=2×8!/10!=1/45.
The union probability is 1/5+1/5−1/45=17/45.

problems.title: Radical equalities impose quadrants
problems.question: Solve √(sinx cos y)=√(−sinx)√(−cos y) and √(cosx siny)=√(cosx)√(siny), given sin2x sin2y≠0.
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: The separate real radicals require sinx≤0,cosy≤0,cosx≥0,siny≥0. The nonzero condition makes every inequality strict.
steps: Thus x is in quadrant IV and y in quadrant II. On those quadrants the product-root identities are valid, so the conditions are also sufficient.
problems.answer: $x\in(-\pi/2+2\pi k,2\pi k),\quad y\in(\pi/2+2\pi n,\pi+2\pi n),\ k,n\in\mathbb Z$.

problems.title: A reflected sine need not be periodic
problems.question: Which is not periodic: cos|3x|,cos²3x,|cos3x|,sin²3x,|sin3x|,sin(3|x|)?
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: Cosine is even; squares and absolute values of the ordinary sine/cosine retain periods.
steps: Only sin(3|x|) fails. A positive period T would have to be 2πk/3 on positive inputs. At x=−π/6 the value is 1, but at x+T>0 it would be −1.
The contradiction excludes every such positive period.

problems.title: Count all roots including interval endpoints
problems.question: How many roots of sin2x=sin3x lie in [0,2π]?
problems.idea: Use the exact identity, counting rule or geometric cross-section and verify restrictions.
formulas: $\sin3x-\sin2x=2\cos(5x/2)\sin(x/2)$.
steps: sin(x/2)=0 gives endpoints x=0,2π. The cosine factor gives x=π/5,3π/5,π,7π/5,9π/5.
These seven values are distinct and exhaust the interval roots.
